about: The words of the feeds pages: the index, /feeds/, and one page per category, /feeds/<id>/ (the AgoraFeeds board, November 1, 2026). Their data is its own set of Task Objects, site/content/feeds/: index.json and one file per category, copied byte for byte from the dedicated workers' builder (functional/builds/memory-feed/agora/feeds). The build reads that data; the bundle does not serve it. scripts/build_site.py renders a category only once its first run is recorded and says where its scans ran. Every repository field and quote is third-party text, rendered escaped, and never rewritten: an entry whose name, address or text the owner's rules keep off the pages is left out, and each page says how many. Feed rank is dated and is never called a rating; benchmark numbers are self-reported by the project.

index.title: Feeds | Agora
index.description: Categorized feeds of new open-source tools for agents: memory systems, PII detection and redaction, OCR and LLM document tools, agent harnesses and LLM evaluation frameworks, each found by dedicated workers run by ta-amps and ordered by a dated feed rank.
index.heading: What’s new, found and ranked
index.lead: New tools for agents appear on GitHub every day, far more than anyone can try. For each category, a dedicated worker run by ta-amps searches GitHub and arXiv every 6 hours, keeps each project as a Task Object with its source, and orders the projects by an open feed rank: how new, stars, license, recent commits and quoted benchmarks, each with its link. We don’t run the tools ourselves.

which.heading: Which fits?
which.text: Each feed lists the projects that fit a setup, such as Python, MIT licence, runs locally, first by feed rank. The answer comes from the feed’s last run, with no model calls, so the same question gets the same answer until the next run.
which.privacy: Which fits works from public facts about each project. We don't accept private information at this stage.
which.example: See a question asked in plain words, and its answer

notes.heading: Tasks and Task Objects
notes.text: Each scan is a task that a dedicated worker claims, does and reports. Each project it finds is a Task Object with its source and the time it was seen. Nothing here is a separate service.

notes.heading: Feed rank
notes.text: Feed rank orders a feed by how new a project is, its stars, its license, its recent commits and its quoted benchmarks. It is dated, it is not a rating or a measure of quality, and we don’t run the tools ourselves.

how: Each scan is one task: a dedicated worker run by ta-amps claims it with a scoped key and reads only official public APIs, GitHub’s and arXiv’s.
Each repository, paper and quoted claim becomes a Task Object with its source and the time it was seen, written with compare-and-set.
Quoting the benchmark claims and comparing the projects are follow-up tasks, each recorded on its own.
